memo.thesis_en: I own three shares of Accenture, bought four days ago at $251.845, and they are now $226.12, down 10.21%. A price drop of that size, with nothing in the filings telling me the franchise has changed, is not a reason to sell; my own rules say it is the kind of thing to ignore. The snapshot shows a five-year average ROE of 26.9% and debt-to-equity of 0.32, which is the profile of a business earning good returns without leaning on leverage. The model's intrinsic value of $437.57 rests on an 8% growth cap and a 5% discount rate, and I would not lean on a 49% margin of safety built on assumptions that generous. The real question is whether the consulting and outsourcing relationships stay sticky as technology shifts, and I can't prove that from this data, so I keep the position at modest size and keep my eyes open.

memo.thesis_en: I own this one, so the question is whether to keep it, and on the evidence I have, I keep it. The snapshot shows a 5-year average ROE of 23.8%, debt-to-equity of 0.40, and a price of $212.82 against an owner-earnings value of $260.01. The snapshot says nothing about ten years of earnings history, CEO tenure or ROIC, so I can't call this a wonderful business, only a good one at a fair price. I'll hold, I won't add until the moat evidence improves, and I won't sell on a 1.8% paper loss. Price declines are not a sell trigger.

memo.two_paragraph_business_description:
MSC Industrial Direct distributes metalworking tools, cutting tools, abrasives, fasteners and other maintenance, repair and operations supplies to manufacturers and industrial customers. It buys from thousands of suppliers and sells through catalogs, a website, branch locations and on-site inventory programs.

It makes money on the spread between what it pays suppliers and what it charges customers, and it earns that spread by being fast, reliable and broad in selection. The customer is buying uptime, because a broken machine tool costs more than the part. That lets a good distributor hold its margin, while the capital needs stay modest relative to earnings.
